corroborated_findings.finding: The `pressure` load was documented "MPa, inward" but a POSITIVE magnitude loaded the surface along its OUTWARD normal, so on a bore +p was EXTERNAL pressurisation and internal pressure needed a negative magnitude. The code was wrong, not the docs: +p pushing INTO the surface is the universal convention, is what run_fea_static / cad_guide document, and is what the render annotation already quotes (p*A "N inward").
corroborated_findings.evidence: Measured on the Lame cylinder (a=15, b=30, L=90 mm, tet4): pressure=+20 MPa on the bore gave sigma_hoop = -29.6 MPa (hoop COMPRESSION) and u_r < 0 against Lame's +33.33 MPa; pressure=-20 MPa on the identical model reproduced the closed form. Root cause: the deposit was +p*integral(N_i n_outward)dA in core/sim/fea_run.cpp (fea_run_static_impl, the `type == "pressure"` branch) with the outward orientation explicitly enforced. Fixed on 2026-09-05: the deposit is now -p*integral(N_i n_outward)dA, so +p acts inward, and this case passes +p. Force loads were never affected.

corroborated_findings.case: PLATE-HOLE (tet4 stress recovery at a concentration)
corroborated_findings.finding: On tet4 — whose element stress really is constant, so nodal averaging is the only recovery available — nodal stress under-recovers the Kirsch peak at a hole rim, and does so non-monotonically: the SCF is a lower bound at these mesh sizes, so a peak stress read off a graded tet4 mesh at a stress concentration is optimistic. This is the one analytic row this harness leaves FAILING, deliberately. The tet10 half of this finding was a solver defect and is FIXED — see the 'PLATE-HOLE / tet10 stress recovery' entry.
corroborated_findings.evidence: 200x100x5 mm plate, d=10 mm central hole, gross sigma_inf 10 MPa, reference Kirsch 3.00 / Howland 3.03. Measured max nodal sigma_xx on the rim: tet4 1.62 -> 2.39 -> 2.75 -> 2.64 over h_eff 2.87/2.59/2.18/1.96 mm (finest 12% low, and NOT monotone). That non-monotonicity is the MESH FAMILY, not the recovery: CalculiX C3D4, handed the identical four meshes, reports 1.6153 / 2.3872 / 2.7535 / 2.6419 — the same numbers to ccx's 6-digit print floor, including the same drop at the finest leg, because the graded-tet ladder is not a nested family. The far-field stress on the same solves is right to 6e-4..2e-3, so the load path and the solve are fine, and the practical rule is: do not quote a peak stress at a concentration without refining until the SCF stops moving.

corroborated_findings.case: CYL-LAME (reaction resultant is degenerate for a self-equilibrated load)
corroborated_findings.finding: The reaction-resultant cross-check is meaningless when the applied load has zero resultant, and on those legs the ccx RF sum over the fixed set is non-zero and mesh-dependent while Chudware reports exactly zero. Left as an OPEN reaction-bookkeeping question, not a solution difference.
corroborated_findings.evidence: Internal pressure on a bore is purely radial, so the true resultant is 0. Chudware reaction_force_n = [0,0,0] on all four tet4 legs and both tet10 legs; the ccx *NODE PRINT RF sum over NFIX gives Fz = -182.85, 0.54, 250.27, 192.86 N (tet4 h=24/20/13/9.5) and 15.14, 0.00 N (tet10 h=24/20) — erratic in mesh, so it is not a load the model carries. The displacement fields on those SAME meshes agree node-for-node at |u| L2 1.63e-07..1.72e-07, i.e. at ccx's own print precision, so the solutions are identical and the discrepancy lives in the reaction reporting (or in this harness's parse of ccx's RF table), not in the solve. On the 21 force-loaded meshes the same comparison agrees to 1.88e-07 worst case, which is why the metric is kept.

corroborated_findings.case: PLATE-HOLE / tet10 stress recovery (ROOT-CAUSED, FIXED, RE-MEASURED)
corroborated_findings.finding: The tet10 hole-rim SCF under-recovery first reported as an open finding was a real defect in tet10 Gauss-point -> nodal stress recovery, not a mesh-resolution limit: the recovery collapsed the 4 Gauss points of a tet10 to an ELEMENT CONSTANT before nodal averaging, which is why tet10 read WORSE than tet4 at the rim on the same geometry. Recovery now extrapolates the 4 Gauss-point tensors to the corner nodes (the mid-edge nodes take the mean of their two corners) — the same recovery CalculiX uses for C3D10. tet4 and hex8 are untouched and their numbers are unchanged.
corroborated_findings.evidence: Diagnosed off this harness's Tier-2 lane, which hands CalculiX the identical mesh. BEFORE / AFTER / ccx C3D10 on the SAME mesh, rim SCF: h_eff 3.445 (20664 elems) 1.46607 / 2.22806 / 2.2280; h_eff 2.870 (35744) 1.75700 / 2.57926 / 2.5792; h_eff 2.586 (48880) 2.43741 / 3.44426 / 3.4442; and on the old finest mesh (73072 elems, h_eff 2.261) 2.17568 / 3.16604 / 3.1660. After the fix Chudware reproduces ccx's own C3D10 nodal stress to its 6-digit print floor on every one of those meshes, and tet4 was already exact against C3D4 (1.6153 both), which localised the defect to the quadratic recovery path alone. The re-run finest tet10 leg (81928 elems, h_eff 2.177, a slightly finer mesh than the old run, whose leg was coarsened by a tighter memory envelope) reads SCF 3.08792 against ccx 3.08790 on that mesh: 2.9% from Kirsch 3.00 and 1.9% from Howland 3.03, so the row PASSES, and the error against the finite-width reference now falls at EVERY refinement (0.265 -> 0.149 -> 0.137 -> 0.019, monotone=True). The displacement rows were never affected (Tier 2 agreed to ~1e-07 on these same meshes) — only nodal STRESS at a gradient was wrong. Fixed in core/sim/fea_static.cpp; pinned by the core ctest `sim` case "tet10 nodal stress recovery reports the extreme-fibre bending stress", which reads 301.4 MPa against M c/I = 300 MPa where the element-constant recovery read 247.7 MPa.

corroborated_findings.case: CYL-LAME post-fix spot measurement (supersedes the Lame rows in the tables)
corroborated_findings.finding: With BOTH fixes in (pressure sign + tet10 Gauss-point stress recovery) the Lame case is far more accurate than the tables in this report show, and the sign question is settled by measurement: pressure=+p IS internal pressurisation on a bore. The tables above were measured before either fix; the numbers here are the current engine.
corroborated_findings.evidence: Measured through this harness's own chud_solve/extract on the identical CYL-LAME model (a=15, b=30, L=90 mm), engine carrying the tet10 recovery fix. tet10 h_req=16 (56840 elems), pressure=+p: hoop inner +33.0205 MPa vs Lame +33.3333 (-0.94%), hoop outer +13.2720 vs +13.3333 (-0.46%), u_r inner +0.00291 mm (-1.39%). The -p probe mirrors it exactly negative (-33.0205 / -13.2720), which is the sign convention pinned as data rather than read off a docstring. tet4 h=20: hoop outer +13.3678 (+0.26%), hoop inner +27.23 (-18.3%) — the tet4 rim under-read, NOT a sign error. Compare the pre-fix tet10 rows in Tier 1 (hoop inner 8.55% low): that gap was the tet10 recovery defect, not the Lame model or the mesh. Engine convention is now f_i = -p*integral(N_i n_outward) dA, i.e. +p pushes INTO the face as its contract always claimed.

corroborated_findings.case: provenance.engine_build_id is NOT unique per build (harness/provenance defect)
corroborated_findings.finding: A `-dirty` build id does not identify a build. This report's central integrity check was "every row carries the same engine_build_id, so the table cannot straddle two builds" — that check is WEAKER than claimed: the id is a git describe of a dirty working tree, so a rebuild with real code changes produces the IDENTICAL string. Rows measured before and after a solver fix are therefore indistinguishable by build id alone.
corroborated_findings.evidence: Demonstrated inside this very report. The PLATE-HOLE tet10 rim SCF rows were re-measured after the tet10 stress-recovery fix and now read 2.22806 / 2.57926 / 3.44426 / 3.08792 (was 1.46607 / 1.75700 / 2.43741 / 2.17568), yet every one still carries engine_build_id `beta-0.1.2-beta.41-80-gfac9a08ab-dirty`, the same string as the pre-fix rows. What actually distinguishes them is the `reruns` record in fea_vv_results.json (case, tiers, reason, command, generated_utc), which is why that record is load-bearing evidence and not bookkeeping. FIX for the engine: make the build id carry a content hash of the built artifact (or a dirty-tree digest) so two different binaries can never share an id — sim results are only evidence-grade if their provenance is injective.

corroborated_findings.case: Mixed-recovery stress columns in this report (read-me-first caveat)
corroborated_findings.finding: After the targeted PLATE-HOLE re-run, this report's nodal-STRESS columns are no longer all from one recovery implementation: PLATE-HOLE Tier-1 tet10 rows are post-fix, while tet10 nodal-stress columns elsewhere (Tier-2 peak von Mises) still reflect the OLD element-constant recovery and will move UP on a full refresh. Displacements and reactions are unaffected anywhere.
corroborated_findings.evidence: Confirmed by the targeted re-run. The fix extrapolates the 4 Gauss-point tensors to corner nodes (corner_i = sqrt(5)*(g[i] - b*sum g), mid-edges as the mean of their two corners) — CalculiX's own C3D10 recovery — and tet4/hex8 are bit-identical. Same-mesh agreement on STRESS is now essentially exact: Chudware 2.22806/2.57926/3.44426/3.08792 vs ccx 2.2280/2.5792/3.4442/3.08790 at h_eff 3.445/2.870/2.586/2.177, so the finest tet10 SCF row PASSES (2.9% vs Kirsch 3.0, 1.9% vs Howland 3.03) and the Howland error now falls at every refinement. A regression case in core/tests/test_sim.cpp pins tet10 extreme-fibre nodal sigma_xx 301.4 vs M c/I 300 (the old recovery read 247.7).
